bull_bear.body: Dividend of INR 3.5/share recommended. Funding mix for future capex: Internal accruals, unutilized DFI (Proparco) limits, and potential sale of unsold EPR credits. No immediate equity dilution planned despite expired QIP approval.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical volatility affecting energy/logistics costs; US trade policy shifts impacting indirect exports via SE Asia; Cheap Chinese virgin polymer imports undercutting recycled plastics; Delays in PCB approvals for EPR credit accrual on Pyrolysis units.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges FY26 as a 'transition year' with absorbed costs; emphasizes 'inflection point' for FY27; confident in long-term circular economy thesis and operational leverage from new assets.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management revealed that indirect exports to SE Asia (for tires sold to US) have not fully recovered despite direct US volume recovery; TPO pricing correlates with fuel oil but volume is constrained by bitumen shortage in road construction due to West Asia conflict; EPR credits for Pyrolysis (accruing retrospectively upon approval) could provide a significant one-time earnings boost in H1 FY27.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Trusted supplier to 8 of the top 10 global tyre manufacturers, serving 400+ customers globally
- Recycling capacity exceeding 122,000 MTA across 8 manufacturing units
- Sourcing network spanning 150+ cities and a global presence in 55+ countries, supporting reliable input availability at scale
- Early investment in in-house bio-based fuel heating systems and solar power, insulating operations from fuel/energy cost volatility and supply disruptions
- Technology leadership in reclaim rubber - developed a next-generation low-GHG emission production line and replaced 32-38% of traditional reclaim capacity with new technology during the year, improving cost and energy efficiency
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Global trade volatility — Container shortages, rising freight costs, and geopolitical tensions could affect timely delivery and export margins; mitigated through geographic diversification and greater domestic-market focus.
- Raw material price volatility and availability — Fluctuations in raw material prices and supply chain disruptions pose risks to cost management and production timelines, requiring proactive sourcing strategies and supplier diversification.
- Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) policy execution risk — Although overall risk has reduced with greater regulatory clarity on pricing and a more stable EPR portal, implementation gaps in the policy framework, presence of non-compliant recyclers, external stakeholder dependencies, demand-supply imbalances, and delays with the plastics EPR portal continue to create operational uncertainty.
- Sub-optimal capacity utilisation at GCSL — Despite a successful launch and major customer approvals, GRP Circular Solutions Limited (Repurposed Polyolefins) is currently operating below optimal capacity due to delays in scaling operations and supply chain bottlenecks.
- Pace of technology adoption — Significant technology projects are underway (SAP system upgrades, DMS, shopfloor digitisation), but the pace of execution needs to accelerate to match the scale of the Company's growth ambitions.
- Key managerial personnel vacancy — The Company Secretary & Compliance Officer resigned effective 7th April 2026; the search for a replacement was under active progress as of the report date, leaving a KMP compliance role temporarily vacant.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Reclaim Rubber: Export volumes -15%, Domestic +10%; margins pressured by 43% RM inflation in specific SKUs and lower-margin domestic mix. Pyrova Energy (Pyrolysis): Commissioned in H2; operating at >85% utilization; currently selling TPO to road/industrial fuel; rCB facility expected H2 FY27. Engineering Plastics: Automotive segment showing strong traction; Packaging segment pressured by cheap Chinese virgin PP imports. Polymer Composite: Discontinued due to weak viability/tariffs.

business.body: GRP is an integrated polymer/rubber recycling company operating across Reclaim Rubber, Engineering Plastics, Repurposed Polyolefins (via wholly owned subsidiary GRP Circular Solutions Limited), Polymer Composite & Custom Die-Forms, and Waste-to-Energy (branded Pyrova Energy) verticals. It serves over 400 customers globally, including 8 of the top 10 global tyre manufacturers, supplying materials used in tyre and automotive component manufacturing, ground transportation, agricultural and earth-moving equipment, packaging, and increasingly petrochemicals and infrastructure applications.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Reclaim Rubber:** Reclaim rubber grades, including a newly commercialised next-generation low-GHG emission production line
- **Engineering Plastics:** Tire-cord-derived engineering plastics, Grades developed from ocean plastics (fishnet waste) and textile waste
- **Repurposed Polyolefins (GRP Circular Solutions Ltd):** Recycled polypropylene and polyethylene materials from rigid end-of-life packaging waste
- **Polymer Composite & Custom Die-Forms:** Polymer composite products (contract manufacturing discontinued/wound down in Q3 FY26), Custom die-form products for agricultural and earth-moving equipment
- **Waste-to-Energy:** Pyrova Energy - continuous pyrolysis outputs from crumb rubber (feeding petrochemicals, tyre & rubber manufacturing, pigments, paints & coatings, and plastics industries)

latest_quarter.body: FY26 margins compressed by raw material inflation (up to 43% in some SKUs), unfavorable product mix (shift to lower-margin domestic sales), and start-up costs of Pyrova. Pricing pass-through for RM inflation fully implemented from April 2026.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Expect restoration of export volumes in FY27; Domestic growth continuing. Margins: Reclaim Rubber margins to recover as export mix improves (exports are ~200-250bps higher margin); Pyrova Energy targeting high double-digit EBITDA margins upon full stabilization (FY28). Order Inflow: Stronger than FY26 average. Capex: INR 90-100cr planned for FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Order book described as 'much stronger and higher' than most of FY26 driven by new business wins and North American volume recovery; specific numeric value not disclosed.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Scaling Pyrova Energy to 45k tons pyrolysis capacity and 12k tons rCB by Feb 2027; moving TPO up the value chain from road surfacing to industrial furnaces and petchem feedstock; doubling new-tech Reclaim Rubber capacity to 700 tons/month; increasing circular material content in automotive OEMs.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scale the Reclaim Rubber business through increased deployment of next-generation, high-margin technologies
- Expand the Pyrova Energy (Waste-to-Energy) vertical and operationalise recovered Carbon Black (rCB) facilities as part of the Crumb Rubber-Pyrolysis-rCB value chain
- Build an innovation pipeline anchored on new product launches such as recovered carbon black
- Modernise enterprise technology - upgrade SAP systems, adopt Artificial Intelligence, and expand digital shopfloor automation to lift enterprise-wide efficiency
- Reassess the operating model of the Repurposed Polyolefins subsidiary (GCSL), aligning capital deployment to return thresholds and shifting focus to sourcing efficiency and higher-specification applications (automotive, electricals, appliances)
- Mitigate global trade volatility through geographic diversification and a stronger domestic-market focus
- Manage raw-material price volatility through proactive sourcing strategies and supplier diversification
- Discontinue economically unviable operations (Polymer Composite) and reallocate resources to higher-growth, more sustainable business areas
- Dividend recommendations are linked to annual performance - the Board recommended a dividend of Rs.3.50 per equity share (35%) for FY26, down from Rs.14.50 per share (145%) in FY25, tracking the year's profit decline; the Board also decided not to transfer any amount to reserves for the year under review.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: GRP commissioned its Crumb Rubber and Continuous Pyrolysis facilities in Solapur during the year - Phase 1 of the company's ELT-to-Energy initiative - with further integration into recovered Carbon Black (rCB) planned as a next phase. The platform was commercialised under the new brand 'Pyrova Energy', housing India's largest single-line continuous reactor with a capacity to process over 30,000 MT of crumb rubber annually, serving petrochemicals, tyre and rubber manufacturing, pigments, paints & coatings, and plastics end-markets; initial ramp-up saw first-of-its-kind teething issues but commercialisation is described as a foundation for future scale-up. During the year the company invested about Rs.4,237 lakhs in capex (Plant and Machinery Rs.2,451 lakhs, Civil Infrastructure Rs.1,504 lakhs, Others Rs.282 lakhs), with major initiatives being strategic investments in Pyrova Energy, automation across Reclaim Rubber operations, development of low-GHG reclaim rubber processes, and a new product line aimed at higher substitution ratios in customer formulations. This capex plan is partly funded by an External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) of up to EUR 12 million secured from PROPARCO (France), of which EUR 7.5 million had been drawn by end-FY26, with the balance to be availed in phases, mainly supporting Pyrova Energy's development and expansion. Separately, an 8 MW solar power project under PPA for the Gujarat plants is being operationalised, expected to commission in September 2026, in line with the company's target of 50% renewable energy usage by 2028. The Repurposed Polyolefins subsidiary (GRP Circular Solutions Limited / GCSL) operates at an annual capacity of 6,000 tons with utilisation gradually ramping up month over month; the company made no capital investment in this business during the year under review, and is cautiously scaling it with a focus on profitability and sustainable unit economics. The unrelated Polymer Composite operations were discontinued and wound down during the year due to US tariff pressure and unviable economics.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Outlook for circular materials remains strong, supported by tightening regulations, rising consumer awareness, and sustainability commitments from global brands
- India's EPR implementation is creating a more structured and traceable recycling ecosystem for tyres and plastics, reinforced by NITI Aayog interventions and Indian Tyre Technical Advisory Committee collaboration on advanced reclaim rubber processes for automotive tyre applications
- Domestic rubber consumption grew 4% in calendar 2025 with tyre-industry consumption stable; reclaim rubber outperformed, growing 7% YoY (15% in tyre applications), creating trade-diversion opportunities the company is leveraging to deepen domestic presence
- The recovered Carbon Black (rCB) sector is entering a new global growth phase, with emerging markets (India, Asia-Pacific) driving demand and mature markets (EU, North America) creating opportunity via policy support and sustainability mandates; standardization initiatives are aiding OEM adoption, non-tyre rubber-goods segments (conveyor belts, auto components) are beginning to commercialize rCB, and in Europe, mass-balance systems are accelerating use of Tyre Pyrolysis Oil (TPO) as a naphtha substitute, with even virgin carbon black makers now seeking TPO/rCB supply
- Recent government measures and GST-linked incentives aimed at stimulating consumption are expected to support recovery in automotive demand, benefiting the Engineering Plastics business with gradual normalisation in offtake
- Global trade volatility - container shortages, rising freight costs, and geopolitical tensions - continues to affect timely delivery and export margins
- Sustained low-cost recycled-polymer imports, particularly from China (now a net exporter), are pressuring pricing and competitiveness in Engineering Plastics and Repurposed Polyolefins
- US tariff developments remain a key external disruptor for Reclaim Rubber, Polymer Composite and Custom Die-Forms customers exposed to the US market
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: GRP Limited navigated a volatile FY26 marked by US tariff disruptions and raw material inflation, resulting in a 3% revenue decline and margin compression, but successfully commissioned its flagship Pyrova Energy platform which positions the company for high-double-digit margin expansion in FY27-FY28 as export volumes recover and rCB operations commence.

risks.note: Container shortages, rising freight costs, and geopolitical tensions could affect timely delivery and export margins; mitigated through geographic diversification and greater domestic-market focus.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and availability
risks.note: Fluctuations in raw material prices and supply chain disruptions pose risks to cost management and production timelines, requiring proactive sourcing strategies and supplier diversification.

risks.risk: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) policy execution risk
risks.note: Although overall risk has reduced with greater regulatory clarity on pricing and a more stable EPR portal, implementation gaps in the policy framework, presence of non-compliant recyclers, external stakeholder dependencies, demand-supply imbalances, and delays with the plastics EPR portal continue to create operational uncertainty.

Despite a successful launch and major customer approvals, GRP Circular Solutions Limited (Repurposed Polyolefins) is currently operating below optimal capacity due to delays in scaling operations and supply chain bottlenecks.
Significant technology projects are underway (SAP system upgrades, DMS, shopfloor digitisation), but the pace of execution needs to accelerate to match the scale of the Company's growth ambitions.

The Company Secretary & Compliance Officer resigned effective 7th April 2026; the search for a replacement was under active progress as of the report date, leaving a KMP compliance role temporarily vacant.

one-line thesis: GRP Limited navigated a volatile FY26 marked by US tariff disruptions and raw material inflation, resulting in a 3% revenue decline and margin compression, but successfully commissioned its flagship Pyrova Energy platform which positions the company for high-double-digit margin expansion in FY27-FY28 as export volumes recover and rCB operations commence.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 5,380mn (FY26, -3% YoY); Q4 Revenue: INR 1,450mn (-10% YoY). EBITDA: INR 429mn (FY26, 8% margin vs 13% prior); Q4 EBITDA: INR 94mn (7% margin). PAT: Reported loss of INR 13mn (Q4); Adjusted PAT INR 46mn (FY26) after excluding INR 14mn Labor Code provision, INR 79lk Polymer write-off, INR 42lk QIP expenses, and INR 41mn forex loss. Order Book: Strengthened in Q4 due to domestic growth and US recovery. Net Debt: D/E ratio increased to 1.15x (from 0.76x) due to capex funding.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Expect restoration of export volumes in FY27; Domestic growth continuing. Margins: Reclaim Rubber margins to recover as export mix improves (exports are ~200-250bps higher margin); Pyrova Energy targeting high double-digit EBITDA margins upon full stabilization (FY28). Order Inflow: Stronger than FY26 average. Capex: INR 90-100cr planned for FY27.
order book & pipeline: Order book described as 'much stronger and higher' than most of FY26 driven by new business wins and North American volume recovery; specific numeric value not disclosed.
segment / subsidiary detail: Reclaim Rubber: Export volumes -15%, Domestic +10%; margins pressured by 43% RM inflation in specific SKUs and lower-margin domestic mix. Pyrova Energy (Pyrolysis): Commissioned in H2; operating at >85% utilization; currently selling TPO to road/industrial fuel; rCB facility expected H2 FY27. Engineering Plastics: Automotive segment showing strong traction; Packaging segment pressured by cheap Chinese virgin PP imports. Polymer Composite: Discontinued due to weak viability/tariffs.
growth verticals / optionality: Scaling Pyrova Energy to 45k tons pyrolysis capacity and 12k tons rCB by Feb 2027; moving TPO up the value chain from road surfacing to industrial furnaces and petchem feedstock; doubling new-tech Reclaim Rubber capacity to 700 tons/month; increasing circular material content in automotive OEMs.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 margins compressed by raw material inflation (up to 43% in some SKUs), unfavorable product mix (shift to lower-margin domestic sales), and start-up costs of Pyrova. Pricing pass-through for RM inflation fully implemented from April 2026.
capex / expansion: Cumulative INR 170cr (FY24-26): ~50% Pyrova Energy, ~30-35% Reclaim Rubber (tech/capacity), ~15% Others (Solar/Wind/Plastics). FY27 guidance: INR 90-100cr. Key projects: rCB facility, additional pyrolysis lines, solar/wind SPVs.
capital allocation: Dividend of INR 3.5/share recommended. Funding mix for future capex: Internal accruals, unutilized DFI (Proparco) limits, and potential sale of unsold EPR credits. No immediate equity dilution planned despite expired QIP approval.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical volatility affecting energy/logistics costs; US trade policy shifts impacting indirect exports via SE Asia; Cheap Chinese virgin polymer imports undercutting recycled plastics; Delays in PCB approvals for EPR credit accrual on Pyrolysis units.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges FY26 as a 'transition year' with absorbed costs; emphasizes 'inflection point' for FY27; confident in long-term circular economy thesis and operational leverage from new assets.
non-obvious takeaways: Management revealed that indirect exports to SE Asia (for tires sold to US) have not fully recovered despite direct US volume recovery; TPO pricing correlates with fuel oil but volume is constrained by bitumen shortage in road construction due to West Asia conflict; EPR credits for Pyrolysis (accruing retrospectively upon approval) could provide a significant one-time earnings boost in H1 FY27.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: GRP Limited is one of India's leading circular materials companies, converting end-of-life tyre, plastic and industrial waste into value-added rubber, plastic and energy products for global industrial customers.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: GRP is an integrated polymer/rubber recycling company operating across Reclaim Rubber, Engineering Plastics, Repurposed Polyolefins (via wholly owned subsidiary GRP Circular Solutions Limited), Polymer Composite & Custom Die-Forms, and Waste-to-Energy (branded Pyrova Energy) verticals. It serves over 400 customers globally, including 8 of the top 10 global tyre manufacturers, supplying materials used in tyre and automotive component manufacturing, ground transportation, agricultural and earth-moving equipment, packaging, and increasingly petrochemicals and infrastructure applications.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- GRP Circular Solutions Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% shareholding); houses all Repurposed Polyolefins operations
- Grip Surya Recycling LLP (Gripsurya Recycling LLP) — subsidiary: LLP with majority stake held by GRP Limited (99.89% partner's capital share)
- Alphanso Netsecure Pvt. Ltd. — related party: Enterprise over which Key Managerial Personnel are able to exercise significant influence
- GRP Employees Group Gratuity Trust — related party: Post-employment benefit plan of the Company
- GRP Employees Group Superannuation Scheme — related party: Post-employment benefit plan of the Company

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Reclaim Rubber: Export volumes -15%, Domestic +10%; margins pressured by 43% RM inflation in specific SKUs and lower-margin domestic mix. Pyrova Energy (Pyrolysis): Commissioned in H2; operating at >85% utilization; currently selling TPO to road/industrial fuel; rCB facility expected H2 FY27. Engineering Plastics: Automotive segment showing strong traction; Packaging segment pressured by cheap Chinese virgin PP imports. Polymer Composite: Discontinued due to weak viability/tariffs.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Reclaim Rubber:** Reclaim rubber grades, including a newly commercialised next-generation low-GHG emission production line
- **Engineering Plastics:** Tire-cord-derived engineering plastics, Grades developed from ocean plastics (fishnet waste) and textile waste
- **Repurposed Polyolefins (GRP Circular Solutions Ltd):** Recycled polypropylene and polyethylene materials from rigid end-of-life packaging waste
- **Polymer Composite & Custom Die-Forms:** Polymer composite products (contract manufacturing discontinued/wound down in Q3 FY26), Custom die-form products for agricultural and earth-moving equipment
- **Waste-to-Energy:** Pyrova Energy - continuous pyrolysis outputs from crumb rubber (feeding petrochemicals, tyre & rubber manufacturing, pigments, paints & coatings, and plastics industries)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Tyre and tyre-component manufacturers
- Automotive OEM supply chain
- Ground transportation and shipping (Polymer Composite)
- Agricultural and earth-moving equipment (Custom Die-Forms)
- Packaging industry (Repurposed Polyolefins)
- Petrochemicals
- Infrastructure
- Pigments, paints & coatings
- Domestic India market
- Export markets across 55+ countries, including the United States and Europe

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Order book described as 'much stronger and higher' than most of FY26 driven by new business wins and North American volume recovery; specific numeric value not disclosed.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Expect restoration of export volumes in FY27; Domestic growth continuing. Margins: Reclaim Rubber margins to recover as export mix improves (exports are ~200-250bps higher margin); Pyrova Energy targeting high double-digit EBITDA margins upon full stabilization (FY28). Order Inflow: Stronger than FY26 average. Capex: INR 90-100cr planned for FY27.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Scaling Pyrova Energy to 45k tons pyrolysis capacity and 12k tons rCB by Feb 2027; moving TPO up the value chain from road surfacing to industrial furnaces and petchem feedstock; doubling new-tech Reclaim Rubber capacity to 700 tons/month; increasing circular material content in automotive OEMs.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Outlook for circular materials remains strong, supported by tightening regulations, rising consumer awareness, and sustainability commitments from global brands
- India's EPR implementation is creating a more structured and traceable recycling ecosystem for tyres and plastics, reinforced by NITI Aayog interventions and Indian Tyre Technical Advisory Committee collaboration on advanced reclaim rubber processes for automotive tyre applications
- Domestic rubber consumption grew 4% in calendar 2025 with tyre-industry consumption stable; reclaim rubber outperformed, growing 7% YoY (15% in tyre applications), creating trade-diversion opportunities the company is leveraging to deepen domestic presence
- The recovered Carbon Black (rCB) sector is entering a new global growth phase, with emerging markets (India, Asia-Pacific) driving demand and mature markets (EU, North America) creating opportunity via policy support and sustainability mandates; standardization initiatives are aiding OEM adoption, non-tyre rubber-goods segments (conveyor belts, auto components) are beginning to commercialize rCB, and in Europe, mass-balance systems are accelerating use of Tyre Pyrolysis Oil (TPO) as a naphtha substitute, with even virgin carbon black makers now seeking TPO/rCB supply
- Recent government measures and GST-linked incentives aimed at stimulating consumption are expected to support recovery in automotive demand, benefiting the Engineering Plastics business with gradual normalisation in offtake
- Global trade volatility - container shortages, rising freight costs, and geopolitical tensions - continues to affect timely delivery and export margins
- Sustained low-cost recycled-polymer imports, particularly from China (now a net exporter), are pressuring pricing and competitiveness in Engineering Plastics and Repurposed Polyolefins
- US tariff developments remain a key external disruptor for Reclaim Rubber, Polymer Composite and Custom Die-Forms customers exposed to the US market

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: FY26 margins compressed by raw material inflation (up to 43% in some SKUs), unfavorable product mix (shift to lower-margin domestic sales), and start-up costs of Pyrova. Pricing pass-through for RM inflation fully implemented from April 2026.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend of INR 3.5/share recommended. Funding mix for future capex: Internal accruals, unutilized DFI (Proparco) limits, and potential sale of unsold EPR credits. No immediate equity dilution planned despite expired QIP approval.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: GRP commissioned its Crumb Rubber and Continuous Pyrolysis facilities in Solapur during the year - Phase 1 of the company's ELT-to-Energy initiative - with further integration into recovered Carbon Black (rCB) planned as a next phase. The platform was commercialised under the new brand 'Pyrova Energy', housing India's largest single-line continuous reactor with a capacity to process over 30,000 MT of crumb rubber annually, serving petrochemicals, tyre and rubber manufacturing, pigments, paints & coatings, and plastics end-markets; initial ramp-up saw first-of-its-kind teething issues but commercialisation is described as a foundation for future scale-up. During the year the company invested about Rs.4,237 lakhs in capex (Plant and Machinery Rs.2,451 lakhs, Civil Infrastructure Rs.1,504 lakhs, Others Rs.282 lakhs), with major initiatives being strategic investments in Pyrova Energy, automation across Reclaim Rubber operations, development of low-GHG reclaim rubber processes, and a new product line aimed at higher substitution ratios in customer formulations. This capex plan is partly funded by an External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) of up to EUR 12 million secured from PROPARCO (France), of which EUR 7.5 million had been drawn by end-FY26, with the balance to be availed in phases, mainly supporting Pyrova Energy's development and expansion. Separately, an 8 MW solar power project under PPA for the Gujarat plants is being operationalised, expected to commission in September 2026, in line with the company's target of 50% renewable energy usage by 2028. The Repurposed Polyolefins subsidiary (GRP Circular Solutions Limited / GCSL) operates at an annual capacity of 6,000 tons with utilisation gradually ramping up month over month; the company made no capital investment in this business during the year under review, and is cautiously scaling it with a focus on profitability and sustainable unit economics. The unrelated Polymer Composite operations were discontinued and wound down during the year due to US tariff pressure and unviable economics.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges FY26 as a 'transition year' with absorbed costs; emphasizes 'inflection point' for FY27; confident in long-term circular economy thesis and operational leverage from new assets.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Trusted supplier to 8 of the top 10 global tyre manufacturers, serving 400+ customers globally
- Recycling capacity exceeding 122,000 MTA across 8 manufacturing units
- Sourcing network spanning 150+ cities and a global presence in 55+ countries, supporting reliable input availability at scale
- Early investment in in-house bio-based fuel heating systems and solar power, insulating operations from fuel/energy cost volatility and supply disruptions
- Technology leadership in reclaim rubber - developed a next-generation low-GHG emission production line and replaced 32-38% of traditional reclaim capacity with new technology during the year, improving cost and energy efficiency

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical volatility affecting energy/logistics costs; US trade policy shifts impacting indirect exports via SE Asia; Cheap Chinese virgin polymer imports undercutting recycled plastics; Delays in PCB approvals for EPR credit accrual on Pyrolysis units.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management revealed that indirect exports to SE Asia (for tires sold to US) have not fully recovered despite direct US volume recovery; TPO pricing correlates with fuel oil but volume is constrained by bitumen shortage in road construction due to West Asia conflict; EPR credits for Pyrolysis (accruing retrospectively upon approval) could provide a significant one-time earnings boost in H1 FY27.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Scale the Reclaim Rubber business through increased deployment of next-generation, high-margin technologies
- Expand the Pyrova Energy (Waste-to-Energy) vertical and operationalise recovered Carbon Black (rCB) facilities as part of the Crumb Rubber-Pyrolysis-rCB value chain
- Build an innovation pipeline anchored on new product launches such as recovered carbon black
- Modernise enterprise technology - upgrade SAP systems, adopt Artificial Intelligence, and expand digital shopfloor automation to lift enterprise-wide efficiency
- Reassess the operating model of the Repurposed Polyolefins subsidiary …
